label: Rates from 6 April 2026
title: Dividend tax rates for 2026 to 2027: what company directors now pay
summary: The basic and higher dividend rates went up by 2 percentage points from 6 April 2026. What it means for directors who take salary and dividends.
body:
Most owner-managed company directors take a small salary and the rest as dividends. From 6 April 2026 the tax on those dividends went up.

The rates for 2026 to 2027

  • Basic rate: 10.75% (8.75% in 2025 to 2026)
  • Higher rate: 35.75% (33.75% in 2025 to 2026)
  • Additional rate: 39.35%, unchanged

The first £500 of dividends each year is covered by the dividend allowance, and no tax is due on dividend income that falls within your Personal Allowance of £12,570. Dividends from shares held in an ISA are tax free.

What it costs

A basic rate taxpayer receiving £10,000 of taxable dividends above the allowance now pays £1,075 instead of £875, which is £200 more. A higher rate taxpayer pays the same £200 extra on each £10,000.

Who it affects

  • Directors who pay themselves mainly in dividends.
  • Shareholders in family companies, including spouses.
  • Investors with dividend income above £500 outside an ISA or pension.

What I would do

  • Review the mix of salary, dividends and employer pension contributions for this year. Pension contributions paid by the company are not taxed as dividends.
  • Check the timing of dividends near the end of the tax year, especially if your income is close to the higher rate threshold.
  • Remember that you must report dividends above your unused Personal Allowance and dividend allowance to HMRC, usually through Self Assessment.
